title: DevOps / Infrastructure Engineer, part time, ongoing
description:
We are a B2B SaaS company. Our platform runs as three services, application, algorithm and database, and part of our infrastructure runs on DigitalOcean.

We are looking for an infrastructure partner to take ownership of that estate: running it day to day, and building the monitoring, environments and automation that keep it healthy without anyone having to remember to check.

Engagement shape
Part time and ongoing, not a fixed scope project.
The work changes shape over time. The first months are mostly build: monitoring and metrics, test and staging environments, CI/CD, infrastructure as code and containerisation. After that it settles into a smaller, steadier load of operating and maintaining what you built.
We are open to an agency or an individual.

How we work
We hold ISO 27001. In practice that means production changes are planned, scheduled and documented, with a rollback plan, and we approve them before they go ahead. You would implement changes, not approve them, and you would not push to production yourself.
If you have worked in an audited environment before, none of this will be new. If you have not, it is probably not a good fit, and we would rather say so now than after two calls.

What you would run
- Patching and vulnerability management, including emergency patching, with the scan evidence retained
- Configuration baselines and drift detection against a defined hardening standard
- CI/CD pipelines, including automated rollback
- Test and staging environments, and the separation between them and production
- SSH and administrative access provisioning and revocation on our approval
- Firewall and network rules, including administrative access paths
- Log collection and retention, and triage of security alerts
- Backups verified by test restore, which means the restore is actually performed, plus disaster recovery drills
- Certificate inventory and renewal before expiry
- Monitoring, alerting and a metrics stack covering utilisation, latency, throughput and error rates
- Hosting cost, monitored against a baseline, with reductions proposed
- Incident response, including the technical input to a root cause analysis

What you would build in the first months
- A monitoring and metrics stack across all three services
- Test and staging environments, properly separated from production
- Infrastructure as code covering provisioning and configuration, held in our repositories
- Unattended security updates, and patching and hardening baked into the base image and the provisioning path
- Containerisation, starting with the algorithm service
- Written runbooks for every recurring task, and architecture decisions documented as they are taken

What is not in scope
- Promoting releases to production. You maintain the release timeline for infrastructure and environment readiness and tell us when a release can go, and we perform the promotion
- Writing customer facing security documentation
- Completing customer or prospect security questionnaires
- Mapping controls to CIS, ISO 27001 or SOC 2 frameworks
- Owning our risk register or accepting risk on our behalf
- Application development and database administration beyond the operating system and platform layer

Those stay with us. We mention it because the split is not always assumed, and we would rather be clear now than negotiate it later.

What we are looking for
- Strong Linux and public cloud experience on production systems
- Experience working under formal change control
- Infrastructure as code and containerisation
- Clear written communication

Please include in your proposal
- References from comparable engagements
- An explanation of your role and responsibilities on those engagements, so we can see what you owned rather than what the team delivered
- Your availability
- Your hourly rate
